correctness.rationale: Constraints H_j with j>=n have at least n+1 vertices, so below arity n the two ages are identical. At size n+1 only H_n can differ. From the defining failed triples, any embedding H_m->H_n with m<n would have to send 0 to 0 and embed the entire directed m-cycle induced by failures into the directed n-cycle; successor-closure forces the full n-cycle, so no proper such embedding exists. In H_n, 0 is fixed by every automorphism and the positive vertices form a directed n-cycle, hence Aut(H_n) is exactly its n rotations. Therefore one forbidden isomorphism type removes \((n+1)!/n\) labeled structures. Homogeneity identifies these with injective ordered-tuple orbits. Allowing repeated coordinates gives the Stirling transform \(b_k=\sum_j {k\brace j}a_j\), preserving the first nonzero difference. A fresh independent finite reconstruction for n=3,4,5,6 gave automorphism counts 3,4,5,6 and labeled-copy counts 8,30,144,840, matching the symbolic formula; the finite check is corroborative only.
